newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Prudential unit buys Australia pastoral land.
newsitem.headline: Prudential unit buys Australia pastoral land.

text.p: Heytesbury Beef Pty Ltd, a pastoral group owned by Australia's richest woman Janet Holmes a Court, said on Wednesday it had entered an agreement to sell all but one of its pastoral properties for an undisclosed sum.

Heytesbury said it would also sell one of its Northern Territory properties to Prudential Pastoral Co Ltd, a unit of Prudential Portfolio Managers Australia Ltd, which in turn is wholly owned by Prudential Corp Plc.
The companies said in a statement issued by Prudential that both groups plan to jointly explore opportunities to develop plans that fitted both their business strategies.

A Prudential Portfolio spokesman said the acquisition would significantly expand Prudential Pastoral's assets. The pastoral group was launched last November with three properties worth about A$44 million.
Heytesbury, which was formerly one of Australia's largest pastoral land owners, said after this sale it would still own 10 properties in Western Australia and the Northern Territory.
It said its remaining Queensland property Glenprairie station would be sold at auction on May 8.
Following this sale the group would focus on its live cattle export business to Southeast Asia, it said.

"We see the large scale pastoral sector as a significant area of growth and one which provides excellent opportunities for investors over the long term," Prudential Portfolio managing director Ian Horton said in a statement.
Prudential Portfolio has funds under management of about A$9 billion in Australia.
